reason: Live observation showed semantic's actual wall-clock runner initially resident at approximately 712 MiB, below PGR's old 4 GiB foreign-process threshold. PGR could therefore launch during the runner's initialization and contaminate both jobs before memory grew past the threshold.

change.details: Treat every CUDA compute PID as foreign from its first allocation unless it is PGR's exact active child or the exact sleeping semantic cooperative reservation.

safety: The semantic measurement runner blocks PGR even while it is still small.
The cooperative reservation remains the only non-PGR exception.
Manual and queued foreign jobs are never co-run intentionally.
The active-child five-second monitor uses the same fail-closed rule.
